entries.title: Getting a job (the jobs board)
q: how do i get a job
how do i get a job in town
can i work for the village
how do i quit my job
entries.answer: Press U, then The jobs board: the town's openings with their wages, and today's shifts. Press Apply on one.
more: Apply and the employer weighs you like any applicant (standing, skill, citizenship).
steps: Press U → The jobs board.
Pick an opening and press Apply (or take a day shift).
Taken on, your job is a standing shift at its trade: farm hand, woodcutter, shearer, the watch, smelter, hauler, cook, counter hand, healer's assistant.
Work at least three tasks a day: the wage is paid each morning for each day worked.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Ask → Favours → The jobs board
tips: A good week (three and a half stars) brings a rise of a tenth.
Quit any time from the jobs board or the shift card.
warn: Miss three days and you're let go.

entries.title: Paid shifts
q: how do i take a shift
what jobs can i do for coin
how do i get better at a job
entries.answer: Shifts are short paid jobs: serve at a counter, cook, harvest, haul, keep watch. Take one from the Earnings page (U) and follow the card on screen.
more: Take a shift from the Earnings page, a counter's Work tab, the jobs board, or the boss in talk ('Any shifts going?'): once (four hours) or every day.
A card on screen shows the task, a marker and its distance, a par bar, your stars and pay.
Each task is rated one to five stars and paid at once from the treasury.
steps: Pick a job: counter hand, waiter, cook, farm hand, hauler, smelter, night watch or builder's hand.
Follow the shift card: the task in plain words and a marker to it.
Beat par for more stars; mistakes cost a star.
Skill rises Novice → Apprentice → Skilled → Expert → Master: a tenth more pay a level, more tips, and from Skilled a senior post.
controls: [Right-click] the boss → Ask → Favours → Any shifts going?
tips: Happy customers tip out of their own purses.
A town that can't pay doesn't offer the job ('Unpaid').
warn: Two poor shifts in a row bring a warning; three lose a standing job for three days.

entries.title: The Earnings page
q: where can i see my earnings
how do i see open shifts
best prices for what i carry
entries.answer: The Earnings page shows what you've earned and every way to earn here now. Press U, then The Earnings page.
more: The Earnings page (U → The Earnings page, or the town's books → Economy → Earnings) shows your purse, today's and this week's earnings by source, your bank balance and rent waiting, your job skills, and the ways to earn here now: open shifts, wanted orders, the bounty, haul contracts, and the best prices for what you carry.
steps: Press U → The Earnings page.
Press Marker on anything to set an arrow and a column of sparks over the place.

entries.title: Quests
q: what does the gold exclamation mark mean
how do i give up a quest
what is the question mark over a villager
entries.answer: A folk with work for you has a gold ! over its head. Talk to it, press Any work? (Ask tab), then I'll do it.
more: The first giver hands you a Quest Journal: use it for your quests, steps, where to go and how far.
steps: Find a folk with a gold ! (shown to you alone, within about 40 blocks).
Ask → Any work? → I'll do it.
Use the Quest Journal: Under way and Done tabs, each step with a direction and distance.
When a step waits on a folk, its talk screen shows a button for it (Hand it over, a choice).
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Ask → Any work? → I'll do it
tips: You can carry six quests at a time; an offer stands for three days.
Rewards come from the giver's purse or the treasury, and your standing rises.
warn: Giving up (press Give up twice) or missing the day lets the giver down; for a town's quest the whole town cools a little.

entries.title: Quest stories and quest items
q: what is a sealed letter for
what do i do with the parcel
entries.answer: Some quests are stories in chapters with choices, each with its own items to carry. Your Quest Journal says where to go next.
more: Quest items (sealed letters, parcels, peace terms, spy's reports, the smugglers' ledger, the old miner's journal, a wooden toy, a child's drawing, an heirloom ring or locket) are made from the town's own stores and stamped for their quest; carry them where the journal says.
steps: Take the quest, then follow each chapter in the Quest Journal.
Choices matter: accuse the wrong one and it lasts.
Finish a story for the Medal of the Town and a title the folk use (Finder of the Lost, Thief-taker, Curse-lifter).
tips: Each quest item has a recipe, but a crafted one won't do for a quest: the quest's own is stamped with its number.

entries.title: The quest board
q: how does the quest board work
entries.answer: The quest board on the meeting hall lists what the town wants brought or cleared. Right-click a posting to take it on.
more: The quest board hangs on the meeting hall (on the storehouse until there is one) with real postings: Wanted (what the town is short of) and Clear (monsters where it works).
Right-click a posting to take it, again to hand over what it asks for, and once more to claim the reward.
steps: Right-click a posting: your name goes on it.
Bring what it asks (a little at a time is fine) and right-click again.
When it's done, right-click once more to claim the reward.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Ask → Favours → Quest board
tips: Postings you take appear in your Quest Journal.
The elder's current order heads the board.

entries.title: Learning a trade (apprenticeship)
q: how do i become an apprentice
learn a trade from a villager
how do i become a master smith
how do i learn the reinforced pickaxe recipe
how do i unlock the farmhouse pie recipe
entries.answer: Learn a trade from a master (a folk of level 25+): ask it 'Apprentice me' (About, then Work & pay) and do its three lessons.
more: Ask a master (a folk of level 25+ at the smith's, farmer's, miner's, cave dweller's, enchanter's, tailor's, brewer's or cook's trade) 'Apprentice me'.
Its fee is six coins plus one for every five of its levels.
You get an Apprentice's Journal, then three real lessons; each opens a perk, and the last makes you a Master.
steps: Ask 'My lesson' for each lesson and do it with your master nearby (or ask it out with you).
Titles: Apprentice, Journeyman, Master. Use the journal to see what's next.
controls: [Right-click] a master → About → Work & pay → Apprentice me · My lesson
tips: Smith, brewer and cook lessons teach the reinforced pickaxe, brewer's stout and farmhouse pie recipes: only taught players can craft them.
Perks include extra ore, faster crops, a lapis back when enchanting and longer potions.
warn: Away from your master, lesson work doesn't count.

entries.title: The folk's trades
q: how do folk choose their jobs
can i change a villager's job
how do i assign jobs to folk
entries.answer: Each folk takes the trade its town is shortest of, and the elder moves hands where needed. You can ask a folk to change trade in words.
more: Each folk takes the trade the town is shortest of: farmers first, then miners, woodcutters, a smelter, the watch, carriers, a storekeeper, ranchers, fishers, and crafts (smith, tailor, cook, brewer, enchanter...) as it grows.
The elder's orders move hands between trades.
steps: Ask the folk in words: 'take up farming' or 'could you be a miner?'.
It agrees if it thinks well of you (or you're a citizen), the town has a use for the trade, and its own trade can spare it. Once a day each.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → type 'could you be a miner?'
tips: Nobody needs assigning: the town balances itself.
Tell the elder what to order ('we need more miners') to move several.

entries.title: How folk are paid
entries.answer: The town's treasury pays each working folk a wage every morning. The journal's Wages tab (J) lists who earns what.
more: Every morning the treasury pays each working folk its wage: what the job is worth to the town, its skill and level, a little for a hard day's work, times the place (a town pays twice a hamlet's rate).
Short of coin, everybody gets the same share.
tips: What the town made yesterday comes into the treasury each morning as its takings: a busy town pays its wages, an idle one pays short.

entries.title: Night bounties
q: can i get paid for killing monsters
how do i earn coin fighting
entries.answer: After a busy night the town posts a bounty: each monster you kill in town before dawn earns a coin or two.
more: After a busy night (three monsters killed by the folk, or the bell rung) the board posts a bounty: every hostile you kill in or just outside the town before dawn earns a coin from the treasury (two for a creeper, witch, enderman or illager), up to twelve a night, doubled on a raid night.

entries.title: Haul contracts and caravan escorts
q: can i carry goods between towns for money
entries.answer: Haul contracts pay you to fetch what a neighbour can spare; accept one on the Earnings page. You can also be paid to guard a caravan.
more: A town short of something a neighbour can spare pays a player to fetch it: accept on the Earnings page (the fee is held), pay a deposit for the load at the neighbour's storehouse, carry it home and get the fee and deposit back.
Or guard a caravan ('Guard a caravan', Trade → Services) and be paid at the other end.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Trade → Services → Guard a caravan
warn: Not delivered by its day, the load goes back and the fee goes to the town.

entries.title: Interviews for the town's posts
q: how does the town choose a blacksmith
entries.answer: When a post has two or more candidates, the town holds a real interview in the morning that you can watch.
more: When a post that matters (a blacksmith, teacher, librarian, constable, a trade's master...) has two or more candidates, the town holds a real interview in the morning: candidates wait on a bench with their letters of application, each sits before the panel, and the winner shakes hands.
tips: The board, the crier and the gazette announce it the day before.
As a leader, your steward is chosen this way.
